rules.name: Coursework to be completed within the first two years:
rules.desc: Important note: Normally, if a course has the option to be taken as a letter grade, the student must take the course as a letter grade and receive a B- or better to have the course count towards the CSB PhD requirements.

rules.name: Required Courses
rules.desc: Complete the following courses in Autumn Quarter, Year 1.

rules.name: Additional Required Courses
rules.desc: Complete the following courses in subsequent quarters.
rules.notes:
• BIOS 242: Applied Grant-Writing Compelling Fellowships and Career Development Awards (Fall and Spring)

• To be taken once, after selecting a thesis advisor. Students use their Qualifying Exam Proposal and/or skills obtained in this course to apply for fellowships and grants during their time in CSB ( e.g., NIH F31, NSF, etc.). Choose another scientific writing course if you have already secured a fellowship.

• CSB 270: Research Seminar (Fall, Winter, and Spring)

• To be taken fall, winter, and spring of years one and two

• CSB 399: Graduate Research (Fall, Winter, Spring, and Summer)

• To be taken every quarter until students reach 135 units, at which point students have the option to go to Terminal Graduation Registration status and enroll in CSB 802 for zero units all following quarters until graduation

• MED 255: The Responsible Conduct of Research (Fall, Winter, or Spring)

• To be taken once

rules.name: Chemical Biology
rules.notes: If CSB 260 and CHEM 281 are both offered within the same year, you should take CSB 260 for this requirement.

rules.name: Additional Elective
rules.notes: Other electives are possible with approval from the Student Advisory Committee.

rules.name: Departmental Milestones:
rules.desc:
In addition to the university requirements for the PhD described in Graduate Degrees, Chemical and Systems Biology has required departmental milestones:

• The quarterly ethics discussion is required for first and second-year students

• By the time a student is scheduling their thesis defense, the student’s first-author research article should be accepted for publication
